advisory.checklist_item: - [ ] Pin TARGET across the re-exec (carry it in an env var like AUTODEPLOY_REEXEC_GEN) so the re-exec'd process rolls the same commit that was just installed, rather than re-fetching origin/main.
evidence: The re-exec restarts from line 1, so TARGET is recomputed from a fresh fetch rather than carried across exec; the design note in the ticket asserts loop-freedom because 'TARGET pinned', but TARGET is not actually pinned across the exec.
advisory.finding: reexec_if_self_changed re-execs via `exec bash "$SELF_PATH"`, and the re-exec'd process re-runs the full preamble including the unconditional `git fetch` + `rev-parse origin/main` (autodeploy.sh:537-540). If origin/main advances between the first tick's fetch and the post-re-exec fetch, the second process computes a NEWER TARGET than the commit that was just checked out and rsynced, so it rolls a different commit than the one whose body triggered the re-exec — a same-tick TARGET drift.
scenarios: A second commit lands on origin/main during a tick that has just re-exec'd after the source rsync.
advisory.suggested_fix: Export TARGET (and DEPLOYED) across the exec and skip the re-fetch when AUTODEPLOY_REEXEC_GEN>0, or re-checkout the pinned TARGET before recomputing deltas.

advisory.checklist_item: - [ ] Decide whether the reexec cap should fail closed (record backoff / exit 1) instead of continuing and stamping a success marker over a body that could not be verified.
evidence: infra/scripts/autodeploy.sh:514: `err self-update-reexec-capped "installed autodeploy.sh still differs after ${gen} re-exec(s); NOT re-execing again; continuing with the current body to avoid a loop"`
After the cap, the mcp path proceeds to build/tag/flip and later writes mcp-deployed-sha=TARGET, so the marker can again claim a commit whose body was not applied (AC4's exact hazard).
advisory.finding: When the re-exec generation cap is hit (gen >= max), reexec_if_self_changed emits an err marker but `return 0`, so the tick continues to build the container from the current (still-differing, possibly stale) body and then stamps the component marker to TARGET on success — reintroducing, at the cap boundary, the same 'marker reports success over a body that was not applied' condition the change exists to eliminate. It is bounded and loudly logged, but the marker still advances over an unverified body.
scenarios: A pathological case where the installed body never converges to the snapshot (non-idempotent mirror, symlink churn) exhausts the 2-generation cap.

advisory.checklist_item: - [ ] Sweep stale `$STATE_DIR/.autodeploy-self.*` at startup (e.g. before creating a new snapshot) so a hard-kill does not leak snapshot files indefinitely.
evidence: EXIT traps do not fire on SIGKILL; no startup cleanup of stale `.autodeploy-self.*` exists in the preamble.
advisory.finding: The self-snapshot tempfiles `$STATE_DIR/.autodeploy-self.XXXXXX` are removed only by the EXIT trap (or the explicit rm before exec). A SIGKILL / power loss between the `cp` and process exit leaves them in STATE_DIR, accumulating across ticks with no startup sweep.
scenarios: The unit is hard-killed (OOM, SIGKILL, reboot) mid-tick.
advisory.suggested_fix: Add `rm -f "$STATE_DIR"/.autodeploy-self.* 2>/dev/null || true` just before the mktemp.

advisory.checklist_item: - [ ] Add a test that makes the installed autodeploy.sh stay byte-different across re-exec (non-convergent mirror) and asserts the tick terminates emitting `self-update-reexec-capped` at the generation cap rather than looping
evidence: autodeploy.sh:513-516: `if [ "$gen" -ge "$max" ]; then err self-update-reexec-capped ...; return 0; fi`
Commit message: 'a bounded generation carried across exec is a hard stop, so there is no re-exec loop'
search_files for `reexec-capped` and `AUTODEPLOY_REEXEC_GEN` in the test file returned `(no matches)` — no test references the cap or the generation env var

Named violating input: a box whose rsync stub installs an autodeploy.sh that stays byte-different from the snapshot on every re-exec (non-convergent mirror) — no test exercises this, so nothing asserts the cap terminates instead of looping to the 120s timeout
advisory.finding: The newly-added re-exec generation cap (the loop hard-stop) is untested. autodeploy.sh:513-516 adds the `gen >= max` branch that emits `self-update-reexec-capped` and refuses to re-exec again; the commit message promotes it as the guarantee that 'there is no re-exec loop', yet no test drives a non-converging body so the cap fires. All existing tests use the idempotent mirror where cmp converges after exactly one re-exec (generation 1), so a regression that made the cap fail to stop (or off-by-one so it never/always trips) would go undetected.
scenarios: A future edit changes `max=2` or the `-ge` comparator, or removes the AUTODEPLOY_REEXEC_GEN carry-across-exec, silently re-enabling an infinite re-exec loop
